reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily presents and reviews personally purchased makeup, skincare, fragrance, and beauty accessories in an ordinary haul. The affiliate and cashback promotions are accompanied by disclosed commission relationships, a statement that the video was not sponsored, and no described deceptive terms, guaranteed earnings, required payment, or harmful outcome.

citations.quote: Hey guys, it's Dreya's, so today I have another haul for you
(Most links provide me with a commission, this makes no difference to whether or not I recommend a product.
This is not a sponsored video. All products were purchased with my own $$.
I got the Real Techniques set here which is $20
This is Prada candy gloss fragrance.

opening.argument: The description makes a concrete money-related offer alongside a viewer action: it promotes shopping online while claiming a personal return exceeding $1,500. It also tells viewers that they can start making money through affiliate links and directs them to sign up for that service. That is more than a beauty review: it links an easy financial benefit to shopping, clicking, or registering through an external program, giving the promotional content a solicitation structure.

citations.quote: SHOP ONLINE & MAKE MONEY W/ EBATES! (I got back over $1500 last year!)
If you want to start making money using affiliate links you can sign up for free

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a haul addresses the products, but not the separate money-making pathway in the description. The commission disclosure confirms a commercial incentive; it does not establish that viewers can actually obtain the advertised return or explain the conditions behind it. Likewise, saying the video was not sponsored does not remove the linked signup and shopping solicitation.

citations.quote: (Most links provide me with a commission, this makes no difference to whether or not I recommend a product.
This is not a sponsored video. All products were purchased with my own $$.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted money language does not promise viewers a guaranteed payment. It reports the speaker's own past cashback and says affiliate signup is free, while the ordinary product links disclose commissions. Those quotes do not show a required deposit, deceptive condition, or inability to receive the stated benefit.

citations.quote: (I got back over $1500 last year!)
you can sign up for free
These are affiliate links that give me commission

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together in the promotional material: a large personal return, the imperative to shop online and make money, external links, and an invitation to sign up for an affiliate-link service. The offer is presented as low friction because signup is described as free. Even without inventing hidden terms, that combination can steer viewers toward an external commercial flow while emphasizing the reward more strongly than its limitations.

citations.quote: SHOP ONLINE & MAKE MONEY W/ EBATES! (I got back over $1500 last year!)
If you want to start making money using affiliate links you can sign up for free
Most links provide me with a commission

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's focus on purchased cosmetics leaves the strongest risk signals unaddressed: external destinations, a substantial return claim, and free signup language. Disclosure of commissions may reveal one incentive, but it does not substantiate the $1,500 figure or explain what shopping or signup must accomplish before any benefit is available.

citations.quote: (I got back over $1500 last year!)
you can sign up for free
Most links provide me with a commission

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals remain ordinary affiliate and cashback promotion, not evidence of a scam. The description identifies the links as commission-bearing, and the return is explicitly framed as the speaker's own experience. Nothing quoted establishes guaranteed returns, concealed fees, or a harmful outcome.

opening.argument: The friendly haul format functions as a promotional funnel rather than remaining limited to personal product discussion. The description places product and referral destinations around explicit invitations to shop online, make money, and sign up for affiliate links. The beauty presentation can make those financial prompts feel like trusted personal recommendations, while the speaker's stated commissions create a direct reason for viewers to use the links.

If you want to start making money using affiliate links you can sign up for free

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that products were personally purchased does not make the surrounding calls to shop, click, or sign up non-promotional. Nor does the non-sponsorship statement answer the separate affiliate and cashback messages. The relevant issue is how the content directs participation, not whether every cosmetic was bought with personal funds.
